clue.text: 100 and too old for insurance protection

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
over age means older than the permitted limit

explanation.surface: Someone past a hundred is deemed too old to be offered an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the extent of the risks a policy pays out for, the protection it gives the insured.

clue.text: Please write down scheme for avoiding partition

parts.note: O is the exclamation of appeal or entreaty, as in 'O, let me go'
to pen is to write
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A polite request to write down a plan for avoiding the division of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partition' suggests dividing a country, but here it is a dividing wall. 'down' only places the pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan room or office has no internal walls, so its layout dispenses with dividing screens.

clue.text: Muscle former singer used to carry spades

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: used to carry means the singer holds spades within

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A retired singer has been put to work carrying spades, like a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' looks like garden tools, but it is the card suit, abbreviated; 'used to carry' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An extensor is a muscle that straightens or extends a limb, the opposite of a flexor.

clue.text: German certainly seen in an unknown Dutch football team

indicators.note: seen in means the German word appears inside the other letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, as an is
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity
ja is German for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A German fan is certainly spotted among supporters of an unidentified Dutch club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is the famous Amsterdam football club, one of the leading sides in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Swell up? Leg near exploded!

indicators.note: exploded means the letters of leg near are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A leg near an explosion swells up after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' rearranges LEGNEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make or grow bigger, so it means swell up.

clue.text: Petty criminal appearing as the knife is wielded

indicators.note: is wielded means the words as the knife are swung about into a new order

explanation.surface: A small-time crook shows up as a knife is brandished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wielded' rearranges ASTHEKNIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak thief steals by slipping in unnoticed rather than by force, a minor kind of criminal.

clue.text: Reluctance shown by girl taking lead from source in government

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for government

parts.note: the state is the government

indicators.note: the lead from a word is its first letter, here of source

explanation.surface: A girl shows reluctance on taking a leading government role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead from' takes only the first letter of 'source', and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a dislike that makes one unwilling, a reluctance to do or accept something.

clue.text: Privileged pupil engages southern citizen

indicators.note: engages means the pupil takes on and holds the letter within

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton, the elite English boarding school

explanation.surface: A posh schoolboy hires someone from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is England's most famous fee-paying school. 'engages' puts S inside ETONIAN, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian is a citizen of Estonia, the Baltic republic.

clue.text: Game bird returned to new home

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: returned means the bird's name is read back to front

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A game bird is sent back to a new home, like a rescued pheasant being rehoused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' alone is the definition; 'returned' turns SNIPE into EPINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a skittles game in which nine pins are knocked over with a bowled ball.

clue.text: For food, consume lamb at last in shopping centre

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the shopping centre

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
to eat is to consume

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word lamb

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat lamb at the end of a trip to the mall, for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is only a link; 'at last' takes the final letter of 'lamb', and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a small ball of minced meat, a common dish or item of food.

clue.text: Beginning to assess bad experience, having time to drink

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of assess

parts.note: a mare is informal British slang for a bad experience, short for nightmare
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a bad experience and takes time to have a drink to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mare' (from nightmare) is everyday British slang for an awful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Torch left burnt residue in passage

indicators.note: in places left and burnt residue inside the passage

parts.note: a flight is a passage through the air
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A torch leaves burnt ash behind as someone carries it along a passageway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torch' suggests fire, which fits the burnt residue, but it is the British word for an electric hand lamp; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is a portable battery lamp, what Americans call a flashlight.

clue.text: Boy curtailed shout with man entering part of cathedral?

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: entering means the man goes inside the shortened shout
curtailed means the shout loses its last letter

parts.note: to yell is to shout
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A boy's shout is cut short as a man walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' looks like it applies to 'Boy', but it trims the shout; 'entering' signals the insertion. The question mark marks the definition as by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady chapel is a chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary, often found at the east end of a cathedral.

clue.text: Sebastiano in Piedmont town? On the contrary

indicators.note: in says the town's name sits inside the given name Sebastiano
on the contrary reverses the sentence's claim, so the town is in the name rather than the name in the town

explanation.surface: A man named Sebastiano seems to be living in a town in Piedmont.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts Sebastiano in the town; 'On the contrary' flips it, so the town is in 'Sebastiano'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town in the Piedmont region of north-west Italy, famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Suggestion husband ignored: discourteous to butt in

indicators.note: ignored means the husband's letter is left out of the suggestion

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
rude means discourteous

explanation.surface: A wife's suggestion is ignored by her husband, who finds it rude of her to butt in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes H from HINT, leaving INT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in, pushing oneself into a place or conversation uninvited.

clue.text: Wicked inside where tango gives way to foxtrot

indicators.note: gives way to means one letter is replaced by the other

parts.note: internal means inside
Tango is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for T
Foxtrot is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for F

explanation.surface: Something wicked goes on inside where the tango is dropped for the foxtrot, like a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango and foxtrot look like dances but stand for T and F in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means of hell, hence fiendish or wicked.

clue.text: Jam blind mouse would have liked?

definitions.meaning: a long queue of traffic, a jam
the three blind mice in the nursery rhyme had their tails cut off

explanation.surface: A jam that a blind mouse would have welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme 'Three Blind Mice' the farmer's wife cuts off the mice's tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a British term for a queue of traffic stretching back from an obstruction.

clue.text: One making loud calls from severely cold north

parts.note: bitter weather is severely cold

explanation.surface: Something calls out loudly from the freezing far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One making loud calls' sounds like a person, but it is a bird known for its booming call.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a reed-dwelling heron whose booming call carries a long way across marshes.

clue.text: Barsetshire writer to wallow in drink

indicators.note: in places the wallowing inside the drink

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
to roll, as in mud, is to wallow

explanation.surface: A novelist likes to wallow in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' is a verb here, the old word for drinking heavily; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Chronicles of Barsetshire, novels set in a fictional English county.

clue.text: Informer stopped by those working for Resistance

indicators.note: stopped by means the informer is plugged by the other letters

parts.note: a rat is an informer

indicators.note: working means the word those is set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A traitor is caught by members of the wartime Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' looks like the wartime underground, but it is electrical. 'working' signals the anagram and 'stopped by' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current in an electrical circuit.

clue.text: System controls pressure on events at Wimbledon

parts.note: re means on or concerning
sets are divisions of a tennis match, such as those played at Wimbledon

explanation.surface: Pressure builds on matches during the Wimbledon tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London lawn tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Presets are controls on a device fixed in advance, such as stored radio stations on a sound system.

clue.text: Go mad for an alcoholic concoction

definitions.meaning: to lose one's temper or composure suddenly
a mixed drink of spirit or beer with beaten egg and sugar

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy for a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip as a verb means lose control; as a noun it names a frothy drink made with egg and spirits.

clue.text: Something from flora — and from fauna recalled in secluded spot

indicators.note: in places the reversed animal inside the secluded spot

parts.note: a corner is a quiet, out-of-the-way spot

indicators.note: recalled means the animal is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a wolf is one of the animals, an example from fauna

explanation.surface: Plants and animals both show up in a quiet nook of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something' serves both halves: something from fauna is an animal. 'recalled' signals the reversal and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornflower is a blue-flowered wild plant of cornfields, so it is one member of the flora.

clue.text: Writer knocked back one drink at pub, then second

indicators.note: knocked back means the pieces are set down in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ale is a drink
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A writer downs a drink at the pub, then orders a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses I, ALE and BAR to give RABELAI.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Judge almost correct: one would use laser sword

indicators.note: almost means the word for correct loses its final letter

parts.note: to edit is to correct

explanation.surface: A judge almost corrects someone wielding a laser sword.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Wars the Jedi knights fight with lightsabers, the films' glowing laser swords.

clue.text: See in addition the docked canine

parts.note: to eye something is to look at or see it
too means in addition, also

indicators.note: docked means the word the loses its tail, as a dog's tail is docked

explanation.surface: A dog lover points out that the canine has had its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' and 'docked' suggest a dog, but a canine is also a pointed tooth. 'docked' cuts THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye tooth is the pointed upper tooth below the eye, otherwise called a canine.

clue.text: Chance one day to cut stress

indicators.note: to cut means the pieces are pushed into the middle of the word for stress

parts.note: accent is stress placed on a syllable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: By chance one day the pressure is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks like pressure but is the stress on a syllable; 'to cut' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something that happens by chance, without design or intent.

clue.text: This, invariably lethal, used for starters in fight?

definitions.text: This, invariably lethal, used for starters in fight?

indicators.note: in places the first letters inside the fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: for starters picks the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A deadly weapon that is always fatal, brought out at the start of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the first letters and 'in' signals the insertion; the whole clue also describes the knife itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a narrow blade, a weapon one might draw in a fight.
